content.text: I couldn't open any files, so this diagnosis comes from the file list and the usual shape of this NestJS boilerplate. The line numbers are estimates. Please check them against the real code.

candidates.explanation: Most likely cause (unverified). The guard decides who can reach the admin-only endpoints. The symptom is that only the seeded super admin passes. That fits a check keyed to the user's id (for example id === 1) or a hard-coded role instead of a comparison of the user's role id against the roles required by @Roles(). The guard should read request.user.role.id, convert it to a string, and test it against the required roles with includes().

Second most likely (unverified). validate() builds request.user from the JWT payload. If the payload or the returned user object drops or mangles the role for later admins, the guard sees no matching role and returns 403. The seeded user would still pass if it is special-cased or its role happens to match.

Least likely (unverified). The class-level @Roles(...) and @UseGuards(...) decorators on the user management controller. A wrong role enum value, or a wrong guard setup, could block every admin except the seeded one.

fix.description: Make canActivate decide on the user's role and not on the user id. Return true when no roles are required. Otherwise return roles.includes(request.user?.role?.id?.toString()), so any user whose role is admin passes. Also check that RoleEnum values match the ids that the role seed stores.
